justification: The ghost and original express the same semantic core: (1) the golden rule of whole-serving has a vulnerability—whoever defines the boundary of the whole controls what counts as good; (2) a co-equal partner law forbids any node from adjudicating its own boundary unilaterally; (3) this partner law is what prevents the first from becoming a license; (4) it is ratified/settled, not provisional/open. The ghost rephrases all four elements faithfully: 'the one who gets to draw the line' mirrors 'whoever defines the whole'; 'no single part may settle...where the boundary lies' and 'That call always comes from beyond' capture 'no node adjudicates the boundary alone' and 'always checked from outside'; 'could be turned into a permission slip' restates 'keeps the first from becoming a license'; 'unlike the wording...this partner law is settled, not still open' preserves the ratified vs. provisional distinction. Phrasing differs substantially (expanded exposition, different metaphor 'permission slip' vs. 'license'), but semantic payload is complete and faithful. No claims are inverted, dropped, or invented. No structured residual remains.
